Neither inequality implies the other, but both serve to keep the iterated source below M^{-1/2}.

snippet.text:
structure Tally (L s : ℝ) (P : Era) (m : ℕ) : Prop where
  growth : spouse s P (more L s) ≤ Perch.bill (-1/2) s
  stops u (hu : u∈ Icc (s/2) s) : Shelf P.coast m s u
  force u (hu : u∈ Icc (s/2) s) t (ht : t∈ Icc (s/2) s) : Perch.gas P.coast u ≤ Perch.bill (-3/4) s * w t

verdicts.summary: [L] states a different form; neither implies the other.
evidence: [M] prints C_j^{h_t(b)+v_t+2} <= M^{(b+6)/j^2} B_t^{10/j^2} <= M^{1/64}, a bound on the per-step constant over all h_t+v_t+2 steps with an exponent tending to zero in j. [L]'s Tally.growth reads `spouse s P (more L s) ≤ Perch.bill (-1/2) s`, with spouse s P c = (α+1)^c * exp(-3/4 boil s) and more L s = ceil(log(ceil(log s^2)^10)/log L) (the v_t steps), i.e. (α+1)^{v_t} <= M^{1/4} where M = exp((log log s)^2); on_time proves it eventually in s, and covers uses it to keep the iterate below M^{-1/2}, while the first h_t steps are handled inside Peak.launched with no step-count power. No declaration in [L] bounds a constant over h_t+v_t+2 steps or uses M^{1/64} (grep for 1/64 finds nothing in Next/RANK); the two inequalities have different exponents and step counts and neither implies the other, so the claim stands.

[M] prints C_j^{h_t(b)+v_t+2} <= M^{(b+6)/j^2} B_t^{10/j^2} <= M^{1/64}, a single constant-power bound over all h_t+v_t+2 steps. [L] proves in short_step/on_time only (more L s)*log(eager P) <= (1/4)*boil s, i.e. growth over the `more` (v_t) steps by a fixed power, stored as Tally.growth: spouse s P (more L s) <= bill(-1/2) s; the h_t steps and the +2 are not in this bound, and no declaration states the printed all-steps C_j^{h+v+2} <= M^{1/64}. Neither bound implies the other, so the claim stands; it is a different formulation, not a typo in [M].
